I organized the 100 experiments into ten groups. Each group applies one fixed edit to parent cells that differ mainly in a single candidate condition edge, so differences in the measured effect can be attributed to that condition.

| # | Edit | Experiments | Condition being varied |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | e5→conv3x3 | 12 | e3 is none, skip or conv, and whether e5 starts as none |
| 2 | e3→skip | 10 | Rest of the cell is conv-heavy, pool-heavy or skip-heavy, and what op is replaced |
| 3 | e0→none | 10 | Whether node 1 is used downstream (e2, e4), and the presence of e1/e3 |
| 4 | e1→conv3x3 | 10 | Whether e5 is none, which makes node 2 a dead end |
| 5 | e2→conv3x3 | 10 | Whether e0 is none or other ops (node 1 empty), and the replaced op |
| 6 | e4→avg_pool | 8 | e0 op, e4's prior op, and e3 |
| 7 | e5→none | 10 | Whether e3 or e4 still connect to the output |
| 8 | →conv3x3 on e4, e0, e5 | 10 | Which op is replaced (none, skip, conv1x1, pool) |
| 9 | e4→skip | 10 | e3 and e0 status, and the overall op mix |
| 10 | e1→skip | 10 | e5 being none, e2 or e3 status, and the replaced op |
